description: We’re computer science students from Dushanbe Innovation Institute taking on the Field Shift challenge. We enjoy coding and turning ideas into working demos. If you like exploring data, designing apps, or telling a good story in a pitch, we’d love to build something together! 🚀
summary:
ASTERRA is a web tool that helps farmers plan their next three seasons. A farmer draws their field on a 3D globe, answers a few questions, and gets three crop-rotation plans side by side: keep the current rotation, save water, or build up the soil. Each plan explains why it was suggested, which NASA data supports it, the benefits, what is still unknown and what to check with a local agronomist.

The advice uses NASA Earth observations for that exact field: NASA POWER climate and its 20-year trend, SMAP soil moisture, MODIS and HLS vegetation, NASADEM slope for erosion risk, and the GRACE-FO groundwater trend. There is no black box: every suggestion comes from a clear farming rule and shows its data source.
details:
ASTERRA helps a farmer choose what to plant over the next three seasons.

How it works: the farmer finds their field on a 3D globe, draws its outline and answers five questions (last two crops, irrigation, goal, soil, problems). ASTERRA then shows three plans side by side: keep the current rotation, a water-saving plan and a soil-health plan. Each plan says why it was chosen, which data supports it, its benefits, what is unknown and what to check with an agronomist. A table compares them, and a PDF report can be downloaded.

Example from a 28-ha field in the Vakhsh valley, Tajikistan: GRACE-FO shows the region's stored water falling 0.65 cm per year since 2002, so the water-saving plan suggests chickpea and sorghum instead of cotton. NASADEM gives a 0.4% slope, so erosion risk is low. Sentinel-2 shows the soil is bare from November to March, so the soil-health plan adds a cover crop for those months.

NASA data used: NASA POWER (climate and 20-year trend), SMAP (root-zone soil moisture), MODIS and HLS (crop greenness, latest image), NASADEM/SRTM (slope), GRACE-FO (groundwater trend). We used only global datasets, so it works for any field on Earth, not just the USA.

The advice comes from clear farming rules, not an AI model, so every suggestion shows its rule and data source.

Built with Next.js, CesiumJS, Python FastAPI and Docker on our own server. We used Claude Code to help write parts of the code.
